title: Santa Clarita City Council Vector Control Presentation | October 26, 2021

segments.text: mosquito season continues to affect
residents across los angeles county as
temperatures remain high
the greater los angeles county vector
control district's mission is to reduce
the population of public health vectors
and prevent human infection associated
with mosquito transmitted diseases
throughout the county of los angeles
here to present an update from the
greater los angeles county vector
control district board of trustees is
board president and santa clarita
resident heidi heinrich
[Applause]
welcome heidi
thank you so much good evening mayor
miranda and city council members and
staff
i am heidi heinrich the current
president of the greater los angeles
county
director control district and i have had
the privilege of being
the santa clarita's appointed trustee
for the last five years for which i am
immensely grateful
some background for those of you that
may not know i have a bachelor's degree
a master's degree in nursing i'm a
certified public health nurse i'm an
army veteran and i'm a retired nurse
manager with the los angeles county
sheriff's department
the greater los angeles vector control
district was formed in 1952
the mission
was to
protect residents from mosquito-borne
diseases and mosquitoes
the district consists of 36 cities along
with unincorporated areas that neighbor
the district
for a total of serving six million
residents
our mosquito mosquito season is pretty
big here in california
it runs from april to november
although
we can have mosquitoes all year round
because we're so warm
as you can see
this year in santa clarita alone the
districts provided nearly 6 500
inspections based on service calls to
the district they treated over 400
swimming pools and maintained 4 000
storm drains
which are routine maintenance
which are all represented on that map
that one there
we care about mosquitoes because they're
the world's deadliest animal they're
responsible for west nile virus and zika
and there's the potential for community
outbreaks of those diseases
a mosquito's life cycle begins with the
female bite
she needs the protein to lay her eggs
which number between 100 to 350.
within a week those eggs are adults and
the cycle begins again
the best way to break the cycle is by
removing water sources
we have two mosquitoes that threaten our
community the culex mosquito which is
native and responsible for west nile
virus and the 80s mosquito which is
imported from asia and considered
invasive
west nile virus is everywhere in los
angeles county
fortunately in the city of santa clarita
in the last two years we have only had
one positive mosquito and no human cases
when someone is bitten by an infected
west non-virus mosquito
most people have no symptoms
one in five will feel flu-like system
symptoms but one out of every 150 people
will suffer from severe illness and
possibly death
the risk is greater for those over 50
years of age and those with weakened
immune systems there's no vaccination
and there's no treatment for this
illness
the 80s mosquito
is responsible for zika dengue
chikungunya and yellow fevers though
there are no local transmissions of
these they're also responsible for
canine heartworms
they thrive in urban environments both
indoors and outdoors
they breed in very small amounts of
water
up to just two tablespoons
they're also aggressive biters
that will bite during the day and leave
those terrible welts on your on your
legs
the only good thing about mosquitoes is
they don't transmit covid19
no they killed it with another way
so
in addition to vector control district
services there are do-it-yourself
solutions to decrease mosquito
populations a handy checklist can be
found at glacbcd.org
in which you can find
the potential mosquito sources in your
home checklist to kind of look for areas
that people don't think about where
water can accumulate
in closing mosquitoes need water to
breed so eliminating that source will
break the cycle prevent diseases such as
west nile virus zika and dengue fevers
along with wearing insect repellent to
prevent bites
while the district does what it can we
have shared responsibility in mosquito
control
so i encourage you to share this info
with family and friends by using the qr
code up there
or visiting tiptostakeaction.org
for more information on how the vector
control district
can have a greater visibility in santa
clarita
by hosting booths at city events like
concerts in the park please reach out to
our director of communications mary joy
coburn
